analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. The only patch hunk is a comment rewording near head line 4361, outside the visible excerpts, so it has no behavioral effect. I reviewed the visible test excerpts (head lines 610-1755), which exercise the T-041 SSD prefix cache surface:
- Kill switch semantics: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE defaults on and any non-affirmative value disables it.
- The verified weight hash is required.
- The test root requires the ephemeral-key gate.
- The TTL is capped at 1800s, and the env override can only shorten it.
- Disk budget is half of free space, with a 20 GiB fallback.
- Salt isolation, HMAC-tag filenames, corrupt-block deletion, sweep-enforced TTL, LRU eviction, and epoch retention across eviction, TTL sweep and corruption.
- A binding change wipes the root and rotates the epoch.
- Symlink-replaced files are not followed during reconciliation or TTL sweep.
- Write-cap drops and stage pre-floor overflow safety.
These tests are consistent with the documented T-041 mitigations. They do not alter production code, the threat-model assumptions, or any trust boundary. The characterization test at about line 1094 documents that read-time expiry depends on the sweep, which matches the existing description of expiry being enforced only on entries the cache considers expired. I found no concrete security regression or new attack surface. The production sources (SSDPrefixCache, SSDBlockStore, SSDCacheEpochStore) were not supplied, so I cannot confirm they match what the tests assert. That is a coverage limit, not a defect.
